title: The drive-by brake
beat: A camera held out of a car window, pointed 90 degrees left, travelling down Store Street and stopped dead by a hard brake outside the cafe.

invariants.title: Camera never rotates
invariants.rule: The camera stays square to the facade for the whole shot. Vertical edges - piers, doorframes, downpipes - must stay vertical.
invariants.why: A pan rotates about the camera and keeps perspective fixed; driving past changes the viewing angle. Cross-dissolving an oblique plate into a square-on one IS a rotation, and it read as the camera turning to face the next building.

invariants.title: Fronto parallel plate
invariants.rule: The plate must be one fronto-parallel photograph containing BOTH buildings already square on. fb-08-latest-post.jpg, upscaled. Now street_x4_open.png - the same photograph with the cafe's real open frontage inserted into the arch by door_insert.py, which changes what is INSIDE the archway and nothing about the geometry.
invariants.why: Only then is a pure horizontal translation geometrically correct. Any other plate can only ever produce a pan, however fast it moves.

invariants.title: Three phase brake
invariants.rule: Constant speed, then the framing ACCELERATES through the brake, then the return from full lean is faster still.
invariants.why: Phase 2 collapsing early reads as a car accident. camrig's verdict tests it.

invariants.title: Both buildings whole
invariants.rule: Starts square on a complete neighbouring bay, ends square on the cafe bay - piers either side, arch above, shopfront below.
invariants.why: Starting at the plate's left edge cut INSIDE OUT in half; it read as the corner of something rather than a building.
